question: A tap can fill an oil tank in 14 hours. After half the tank is filled, 7 more similar taps are opened. What is the total time taken to fill the oil tank completely?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Time required for 1 tap to fill half the tank = 14 ÷ 2 = 7 hours.

Total taps working on the remaining half = 1 (initial) + 7 (new) = 8 taps.

Time for 8 taps to fill the remaining half = 7 ÷ 8 hours = 52.5 minutes = 52 minutes 30 seconds.

Total time = 7 hours + 52 minutes 30 seconds = 7 hr 52 min 30 sec.

**∴ The correct answer is 7 hr 52 min 30 sec.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by 1 tap to fill the complete tank = 14 hours.

After half the tank is filled, 7 more similar taps are opened.

 
 

 **Tap**
 **Time (hours)**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 1 Tap
 14
 14 units
 1 unit/hour
 
 

 8 Taps
 14/8
 8 units/hour
 
 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total capacity of the tank = 14 units.

⇒ Time taken by 1 tap to fill half the tank (7 units) = 7 units ÷ 1 unit/hour = 7 hours.

⇒ Remaining tank capacity to be filled = 14 − 7 = 7 units.

⇒ Total number of taps working now = 1 + 7 = 8 taps.

⇒ Combined efficiency of 8 taps = 8 × 1 = 8 units/hour.

⇒ Time taken to fill the remaining 7 units = 7 units ÷ 8 units/hour = 7/8 hours.

⇒ Convert 7/8 hours to minutes: (7 ÷ 8) × 60 = 105 ÷ 2 = 52.5 minutes.

⇒ 52.5 minutes is exactly 52 minutes and 30 seconds.

⇒ Total time taken to completely fill the tank = 7 hours + 52 minutes 30 seconds = 7 hr 52 min 30 sec.

**∴ The correct answer is 7 hr 52 min 30 sec.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes & Cisterns Concept

If a pipe can fill a tank in *x* hours, then the part filled in 1 hour is 1/*x*. Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken to complete the total work.

Combined Work Rule

When *n* identical entities work together, their combined efficiency becomes *n* times the individual efficiency, and the total time taken to do the same work reduces to 1/*n* of the individual time.

Time Conversion

To convert a fraction of an hour into minutes, simply multiply the fractional value by 60. To further convert a fraction of a minute into seconds, multiply that decimal or fraction by 60 again.
